examples.business_meaning: Flow Balance is a measure that quantifies the net difference between materials, goods, or quantities received and those dispatched within a given context. A positive value indicates a net inflow (more received than dispatched), a negative value indicates a net outflow (more dispatched than received), and zero indicates equilibrium. It is typically used in logistics, inventory, or pipeline management to monitor imbalances in flow operations.
examples.calculation_explanation: The measure is calculated by subtracting Dispatch Volume from Receipt Volume. Specifically: Flow Balance = [Receipt Volume] - [Dispatch Volume]. Both operands are themselves measures resolved from the same data context, and the result represents the signed net flow.
hidden_logic: The subtraction order (Receipt minus Dispatch) means the sign convention treats inbound flow as positive and outbound flow as negative, implying an inventory or stock-accumulation perspective.

Both Receipt Volume and Dispatch Volume are referenced as named measures rather than raw column aggregations, meaning any filters, aggregations, or transformations applied to those measures are inherited by Flow Balance.
The measure resides on the Flow Entries table, implying that both receipt and dispatch events are recorded in the same table or that the table serves as the unified fact source for both volumes.

examples.business_meaning: A bronze-layer Delta table in the round_two_bronze_20261003 Lakehouse that records individual stock movement events, capturing each inbound or outbound inventory transaction at the warehouse and product level. Each row represents a single movement event with its quantity, date, and type, enabling downstream inventory tracking and reconciliation.
examples.calculation_explanation: The table is a raw ingestion (bronze) Delta table with no derived calculations. It stores one row per stock movement event identified by movement_id, referencing warehouse_id and product_id as foreign-key integers, recording the number of units moved, the event date as a string, and the direction or category of movement via movement_type. Two audit columns (source_modified_at_utc and source_row_version) carry the source system's last-modified timestamp and row version for change-tracking purposes.
hidden_logic: All columns are nullable and carry no default values, suggesting the table accepts partial or incomplete records as part of a landing/bronze ingestion pattern.
event_day is stored as a string rather than a date type, implying the source system delivers the date in a textual format that is not yet parsed or standardised at this layer.
source_row_version is typed as binary, indicating it is likely a SQL Server rowversion/timestamp byte array used for incremental or CDC-style extraction from the source system.
The table name includes 'round_two_20261003', suggesting it is one of multiple versioned or iterative loads, possibly a reprocessing or re-snapshot of the same data set.
partition_index is 0 for all columns, meaning no partitioning has been defined on the table despite its potential volume as a movement log.

examples.business_meaning: Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) aggregated across all subscription plans, ignoring any plan-level filter context. It sums the monthly price of every active subscription regardless of which plan dimension is currently selected in a report, giving a single total MRR figure across the entire plan catalogue.
examples.calculation_explanation: FILTER restricts the Subscriptions table to rows where status equals 'ACTIVE'. SUMX then iterates over those filtered rows and retrieves the related monthly_price from the Plans table for each subscription via RELATED. CALCULATE wraps the expression and REMOVEFILTERS(Plans) ensures that any external filter on the Plans table is stripped away before evaluation, so the result always reflects all plans.
hidden_logic: Only subscriptions with status exactly equal to 'ACTIVE' (case-sensitive string match) are included; any other status values such as 'CANCELLED', 'PAUSED', or 'TRIAL' are silently excluded.
REMOVEFILTERS(Plans) overrides report-level or slicer-driven plan filters, meaning the measure will return the same total regardless of which plan a user has selected in a visual.

The revenue unit is whatever currency and period 'monthly_price' is stored in; the measure implicitly assumes monthly_price is already a monthly figure and does not perform any pro-ration or time-based adjustment.

RELATED requires an active relationship between Subscriptions and Plans; if that relationship were inactive or missing, the measure would fail or return blank without an explicit warning in this definition.

The filter operates via a correlated subquery rather than a simple Top N visual-level setting, giving it precise control over which accounts are included before rendering.

examples.subject: 128b43612d9962a190bb3ef4dab66cd4f4c54c107824a30f1f8a450422c2fc5c
examples.business_meaning: Usage Overage measures the total number of units consumed beyond what is included in a customer's plan. For each usage record, it calculates how many units exceeded the plan's included allowance, summing those excesses across all usage rows. It is used in billing contexts to quantify billable overage consumption.
examples.calculation_explanation: SUMX iterates over every row in the Usage table. For each row it retrieves the related plan's included_units via RELATED(Plans[included_units]) and subtracts it from Usage[units]. MAX(0, …) floors the result at zero so rows where actual usage is within the plan allowance contribute nothing. The resulting non-negative excesses are then summed to produce the total overage units.
hidden_logic: Rows where Usage[units] is less than or equal to Plans[included_units] are effectively treated as zero overage, meaning under-utilisation of a plan does not offset overages in other rows.
The measure assumes a many-to-one relationship between the Usage table and the Plans table, relying on an active relationship for RELATED to resolve correctly.
No time or customer filter is embedded in the expression, so the measure's scope is entirely determined by the filter context applied externally (e.g. by a visual or slicer).

examples.business_meaning: A measure that calculates the total sales amount attributed to the due date of each transaction, rather than the order or ship date. This allows users to analyse revenue performance based on when payment or delivery was due, enabling due-date-driven financial reporting and cash flow analysis.
examples.calculation_explanation: The measure uses CALCULATE to evaluate SUM of Sales[Sales Amount] within a modified filter context. USERELATIONSHIP activates an inactive relationship between Sales[DueDateKey] and Date[DateKey], overriding the default active date relationship so that the date table filters the Sales table via the due date key instead of the standard date key.
hidden_logic: USERELATIONSHIP implies that the relationship between Sales[DueDateKey] and Date[DateKey] is inactive by default, meaning there is at least one other active relationship between the Sales and Date tables (likely on OrderDateKey or ShipDateKey).
The measure does not apply any explicit additional filters beyond the relationship activation, so all existing report-level and page-level filters still apply.
The pattern is a standard role-playing dimension technique, treating the single Date table as multiple logical date roles (order date, ship date, due date) via inactive relationships.

examples.subject: 263c7be9b31b2117681fc4ccdda9f2a0e6eb91b9490e96e86976159907a41dcc
examples.business_meaning: A Power BI report page definition (layout JSON) describing three report pages — Page 1 (Executive Summary), Page 2, and Page 3 — each containing one or more visuals built on AdventureWorks Sales data. Page 1 hosts a pivot table of Sales Amount by Product Category and Reseller Business Type, a map of Order Quantity by Reseller Country, an area chart of Sales Amount by Order Date/Due Date over fiscal months, a fiscal year/month slicer pre-filtered to FY2019, a title textbox labelled 'Executive Summary - Sales Report', and a header rectangle shape. Page 2 holds a similar pivot table sorted descending by Sales Amount. Page 3 holds a smaller area chart of Sales Amount by fiscal month. All pages share the NewExecutive built-in theme layered over the CY20SU09 base theme, and cross-visual drill filtering is enabled globally.
examples.calculation_explanation: No numeric measures are calculated within this layout definition itself. The layout references pre-defined aggregations from the data model: Sum(Sales.Sales Amount) uses aggregation Function 0 (SUM) over the Sales Amount column in the Sales entity; Sum(Sales.Order Quantity) uses Function 0 (SUM) over the Order Quantity column; Sales.Sales Amount by Due Date is referenced as a named measure from the Sales entity. The fiscal date axis is derived from the Fiscal hierarchy (Year → Month) of the Date entity. Row axes in pivot tables join Product.Category and Reseller.Business Type. The slicer carries a cached default filter scoping to Fiscal Year = FY2019. Pivot tables on Page 1 and Page 2 both carry a visual-level filter excluding Reseller.Business Type = '[Not Applicable]' via a NOT IN condition.
hidden_logic: The slicer (visual 75c624f501f3c20eb760) has a cached/persisted filter set to FY2019, meaning the report opens with data pre-filtered to that fiscal year even though the slicer visually shows all years as collapsed (segments 54–60).

The filter excluding '[Not Applicable]' Reseller Business Type is marked isHiddenInViewMode: false, meaning it is visible in the filter pane but was created programmatically (howCreated: 0) rather than by a user drag-and-drop (segments 18–21, 85–88).

Cross-visual drill filtering (drillFilterOtherVisuals: true) is enabled both at the report level (defaultDrillFilterOtherVisuals: true) and individually on every visual, so selecting any data point on any visual will filter all other visuals on the same page (segments 1, 12, 29, 42, 56, 96).

The header rectangle shape (e62f8d740cd4f569300d) uses a ThemeDataColor fill (ColorId 6) with 100% line transparency, acting as a purely decorative branded banner behind the title textbox (segments 68–70).
The title textbox (ddc669d1ed997bf82754) has its background explicitly set to show: false, making it visually floating over the rectangle shape rather than having its own box (segments 65–67).

The pivot table on Page 2 adds an OrderBy clause sorting Sum(Sales.Sales Amount) descending (Direction 2), which is absent from the otherwise identical Page 1 pivot table, indicating Page 2 is a ranked/sorted variant of the same view (segments 78–79).

The area chart on Page 3 uses ThemeDataColor ColorId 9 for the Sales Amount by Due Date series, whereas Page 1's area chart uses ColorId 5, suggesting deliberate per-page colour differentiation for the same measure (segments 97, 43).
The outspacePane is configured as expanded: false at the report level, hiding the filter pane side panel by default (segments 1–2).

examples.business_meaning: AdventureWorks Sales is a Power BI report residing in a specific workspace. It serves as a self-contained analytical report for the AdventureWorks business domain, likely covering sales performance metrics and related data visualisations spread across multiple pages.
examples.calculation_explanation: No calculations are defined within this artifact. It is a report container object identified by a unique ID and workspace ID, with no description provided. Its content is organised into pages (Page 1, Page 2, Page 3) and is subject to legacy PBIR structure constraints meaning embedded query, filter, and interaction semantics are not interpreted.
hidden_logic: The logicalId field is null, suggesting the report has not been assigned a logical identifier and may not be linked to a lineage or promotion pipeline.
The empty description field indicates that no documentation or metadata annotation has been provided for this report, which may hinder discoverability.
The PBIR-Legacy boundary neighbour signals that the report was authored in or migrated from a legacy Power BI format, meaning certain advanced semantic features may be unavailable or unreliable.

examples.subject: 4d91f0636f2a17d6165f9fb96e4c1fd08267d4b5b1f41daae9417f669759ba88
examples.business_meaning: A hierarchical fiscal-date slicer on Page 1 of an Executive Summary Sales Report that lets report consumers filter all cross-filtering visuals by Fiscal Year and Fiscal Month. It is pre-set to FY2019 and exposes a 'Select All' checkbox in Basic mode, making it the primary time-period control for the page.
examples.calculation_explanation: The slicer draws from the Date entity using the Fiscal hierarchy, projecting two hierarchy levels: Date.Fiscal.Year (active, top level) and Date.Fiscal.Month (subordinate level). Both levels are ordered ascending by Fiscal Year (Direction 1). An embedded general filter pre-selects the value 'FY2019' via an In-condition on the Fiscal Year column, so the slicer opens with FY2019 already chosen. Each level is initially collapsed (isCollapsed true) and pinned (isPinned true), giving a compact tree view. The mode is set to 'Basic' and selectAllCheckboxEnabled is true. Because drillFilterOtherVisuals is true, any selection the user makes propagates cross-filter interactions to every other visual on the page.
hidden_logic: The slicer carries an embedded general-object filter that hard-codes 'FY2019' as the default selected value (segments 57-60), meaning first-time viewers always see FY2019 data without needing to interact with the slicer.
Both hierarchy levels are flagged isCollapsed:true and isPinned:true (segments 54-55), so the tree appears collapsed at load time, saving vertical space while still allowing drill-down to month.

The z-order value of 3000 (segment 49) places the slicer above the area chart (z=0) and map (z=1000) but below the pivot table (z=2000 on Page 1 is actually lower—wait, pivot is 2000, slicer is 3000) and below the header rectangle (z=4000) and title textbox (z=5000), establishing a deliberate layering stack.
drillFilterOtherVisuals is set to true at both the report level (segment 1) and on the slicer itself (segment 56), reinforcing that slicer selections will cross-filter all other visuals on the page.

The cachedFilterDisplayItems entry stores 'FY2019' as the display name for the pre-selected scope (segments 59-60), enabling the filter pane to show a human-readable label without re-querying the model.
